providers.title: The formula of Cauchy and Binet
providers.scope: The determinant of the product of a matrix with r rows and n columns and a matrix with n rows and r columns is the sum, over the sets of r indices, of the products of the corresponding minors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The weighted matrix-tree theorem
providers.scope: For a finite connected graph with positive edge weights, the determinant of the reduced weighted Laplacian is the sum over the spanning trees of the products of the weights of their edges.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Inclusion probabilities and covariances of a weighted spanning tree
providers.scope: For the random spanning tree with probability proportional to the product of the edge weights, the probability of an edge e is c_e a_e^T L^-1 a_e, and the covariance of the indicators of two different edges is -c_e c_f (a_e^T L^-1 a_f)^2, which is not positive.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The response identity for weighted spanning trees
providers.scope: The absolute values of the derivatives of the inclusion probability of an edge with respect to the logarithms of the weights of all edges add up to 2 p_e (1 - p_e), which is at most 1/2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lipschitz dependence on the logarithms of the weights
providers.scope: If the logarithms of the weights are changed by at most epsilon, every inclusion probability of an edge in the weighted random spanning tree changes by at most epsilon/2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The determinant identity det(I + UV) = det(I + VU)
providers.scope: For a matrix U with r rows and k columns and a matrix V with k rows and r columns, det(I_r + UV) = det(I_k + VU).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Inclusion probabilities of the uniform spanning tree as determinants
providers.scope: For the uniform spanning tree T of a finite connected graph H and every set F of edges, P(F is contained in T) is the determinant of the entries with indices in F of the matrix K_H = A^T (A A^T)^-1 A, where A is the reduced incidence matrix.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The matrix of the uniform spanning tree is a projection
providers.scope: K_H is the orthogonal projection onto the orthogonal complement of the space of circulations of H; it does not depend on the vertex that is left out.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Circulations are spanned by cycle flows
providers.scope: The space of circulations of a finite connected graph is spanned by the cycle flows.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Convergence of the projections along an exhaustion
providers.scope: For an exhaustion of an infinite connected graph with finite degrees by finite connected subgraphs, the projections onto the spaces of circulations converge strongly to the projection onto the closed span of the cycle flows, and the matrices K_n converge entry by entry to K = I - P_C.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The free uniform spanning forest
providers.scope: For an infinite connected graph with finite degrees there is exactly one probability measure on the sets of edges with P(F contained) = det K_F for all finite F; the laws of the uniform spanning trees of every exhaustion converge to it on cylinders; it has no cycles almost surely, and it is carried along by isomorphisms of graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A tilt is the conditional law given Gaussian observations
providers.scope: For a law on {0,1}^I, a finite set S and t > 0, let Y_f = t X_f + sqrt(t) N_f for f in S with independent standard normal N_f independent of X. Then Y has the density Z_S(t, y) times the product of normal densities, and the tilted probability b_{i,S}(t, Y) is the conditional probability of X_i = 1 given Y.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The response bound for tilts of the free uniform spanning forest
providers.scope: For the free uniform spanning forest of an infinite connected graph with finite degrees, every edge e, every finite set S of edges and t >= 0, the tilted probability of e changes by at most half the largest change of the numbers y_f, f in S.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The neighbourhoods of an edge form an exhaustion
providers.scope: For an edge e = {u, v}, the subgraphs spanned by the vertices at distance at most n from u or v are finite, connected, increasing, and contain every edge for large n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The drift of the free uniform spanning forest
providers.scope: The drift b_e(t, y), the upper limit of the tilted probabilities of e along the neighbourhoods of e, is a Borel function with values in [0, 1]; it changes by at most half the supremum of |y_f - y'_f| when this supremum is finite; and it respects isomorphisms of graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
